_comment: Paired measurements used to calibrate and validate the CPU estimate.
cycles: measured ON HARDWARE with plaits/cpu_probe.h (DWT cycle counter,
inside the real audio interrupt), read off a --stock-bench firmware.
counts: measured under QEMU's mps2-an386 with the TCG plugin, built by the
same arm-4.8.3 toolchain as the firmware.
MEASUREMENT VALIDITY: the AUX tone readout is only trustworthy on builds
that DO NOT overrun the audio deadline. Under sustained overrun the DMA
IRQ's else-if starves one buffer half and the DAC interleaves every tone
with a frozen fragment, inflating decoded frequencies unpredictably. The
fifteen engines below all ran under budget during the bench sweep, and
their tone readings cross-check against QEMU (k ~ 2.9) and, for the probe
inharmonic-string is the cautionary tale. Its tone reading said 6080
cycles/sample (405%) and launched a long hunt through eight refuted
theories and an apparent memory-corruption mystery -- all of it artifacts
of the broken readout channel on the one engine that sits AT the budget
line. The LED meter (a channel that never passes through the DAC) reads
94-100%, in agreement with the model's 99% prediction. Its cycles entry is
the LED-derived midpoint; treat it as +/-4%.

engines.note: LED-meter reading (94-100% of 1500); the 6080 tone reading was a readout artifact under overrun

_provenance.hardware: Plaits, STM32F373 @ 72 MHz, 48 kHz, block size 12
_provenance.two_engines_merged: virtual-analog and wave-terrain read the same plateau (990); their individual costs are within measurement resolution of each other
_provenance.corrected: 2026-07-27: inharmonic-string re-measured via the LED channel after the tone channel was shown to be invalid under overrun
